name: DROID: A Large-Scale In-the-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
description: DROID (Distributed Robot Interaction Dataset) is a diverse, open-source real-world robot manipulation dataset consisting of 76,000 demonstration trajectories (equivalent to 350 hours of physical interaction) collected across 564 naturalistic domestic and office scenes and 86 tasks. Gathered over a 12-month period across North America, Asia, and Europe using portable Franka Emika Panda arms equipped with two ZED 2 stereo cameras, an end-effector wrist camera, and VR teleoperation headsets, DROID provides rich multi-view stereo observations, proprioceptive telemetry, and updated camera calibration metadata. It serves as a primary benchmark for in-the-wild generalization and large-scale Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy pretraining.

source_references.title: DROID Calibrations & Language Annotations on Hugging Face
source_references.notes: Provides improved camera calibrations for 36k episodes and 3 natural language descriptions for 75k episodes (95% of successful trajectories).

verification.notes: Verified against project website, arXiv:2403.12945, Hugging Face KarlP/droid repository, and GCS bucket gs://gresearch/robotics/droid. Confirmed 76k trajectory count, 1.7 TB payload, and CC BY 4.0 license.

size.notes: Official RLDS distribution in Google Cloud Storage (gs://gresearch/robotics/droid) is 1.7 TB. Raw stereo full-HD footage is hosted at gs://gresearch/robotics/droid_raw.

provenance.collection_method: Distributed real-world teleoperated demonstration collection using portable Franka Emika Panda arms equipped with dual ZED 2 stereo exterior cameras and an end-effector ZED Mini camera.
provenance.curation_notes: Collected across 564 scenes in North America, Asia, and Europe across 86 manipulation tasks. Converted into standardized RLDS format compatible with Open X-Embodiment training pipelines.
data_sources: Independent in-the-wild recordings across 50 data collectors in residential, lab, and commercial environments
